one_line_contribution: On manufactured k=3 retrieved sets in a multi-step ALFWorld agent, the leave-one-out credit of an item is claimed to be systematically biased by one co-retrieved neighbour with a sign fixed by the pair's type (a correct item absorbs >=50% of a planted wrong-procedure item's harm; a paraphrase twin absorbs >=75% of a correct item's help), and a two-player Shapley inside the flagged pair is claimed to fix the resulting pruning error and to match exact k=3 Shapley to within 3 net at 4 re-runs instead of 7.
closest_prior_work: arxiv:2507.04480, 'Source Attribution in Retrieval-Augmented Generation' (verified via s2cli/S2: 2025-07-06, PKDD/ECML Workshops, 7 citations). Its stated aim is to 'quantify how well SHAP approximations can mirror exact attributions while minimizing costly LLM interactions' and to identify critical documents, and the proposal itself concedes it already reports redundancy, complementarity and synergy among retrieved documents. That is the same estimand family (interaction structure among co-retrieved items) and the same cost axis (cheap approximation vs exact Shapley, measured in LLM calls) as P5 and the cost claim; the proposal's differentiator is the transport to a multi-step agent with manufactured ground-truth pairs and a pruning decision, which is a setting change rather than a new claim. Two further verified threats narrow the gap: arxiv:2605.05716 (verified, 2026-05-07) already runs exact Shapley over a 2^5 component factorial in agents and reports 56% submodularity violations, i.e. measured non-additivity with the exact estimator in agent scaffolds, concluding that greedy selection is unreliable; arxiv:2604.05467 CUE-R (verified, 2026-04-07) already runs per-evidence-item REMOVE/REPLACE/DUPLICATE interventions with a role taxonomy. Separately, the two sign predictions are close to textbook in the home literature I searched: that leave-one-out understates value under redundancy and misprices complementary/conflicting members is the defining content of interaction indices and data valuation (Data Shapley arxiv:1904.02868, joint Shapley arxiv:2107.11357, shapiq arxiv:2410.01649, all verified). None of these makes the specific decision-error claim in a multi-step agent, so this is not a collision, but it leaves the contribution as magnitudes plus a setting.
strongest_objection: The decision half of the title is true by construction, not by measurement. The proposal states the identity phi_i = 0.5[(v(FULL)-v(-i)) + (v(-j)-v(-ij))], and separately that phi_W - phi_E = c_W - c_E, i.e. the two-player Shapley is an affine transform of the single-removal credit with an offset of about -H/2 (phi_W ~= 0.5(c_W - H)). P3 then applies the SAME absolute cutoff (-H/3) to both estimators. Under that rule the pairwise estimator deletes W whenever c_W <= +H/3 while single removal requires c_W <= -H/3, so the deletion-rate gap is exactly P(-H/3 < c_W <= H/3), which at the stated per-set SE of 15-18 net is large (tens of points) for every value of I_EW including I_EW = 0. The pre-registered 'falsified if the paired difference is <= 5 points' therefore cannot occur, and the headline 'pairwise deletes W where single removal does not' is produced by a level shift the proposal itself proves is information-free within the pair. The automated entailment check reaches the same conclusion and the proposal's mitigations (noise-only expectation at zero heterogeneity, empirical-Bayes shrinkage, -H/6 and -H/2 sensitivity) do not touch a deterministic offset; sweeping the threshold only relabels which offset is used. Two supporting problems compound it: (a) P5, the claim that pairwise substitutes for exact Shapley, is unconfirmable at the stated power, since the confirming region |D| <= 3 net sits entirely inside the stated D CI of +/-3.6 (only the falsifier at 9 net is resolvable); (b) the cost accounting is wrong for an unflagged set. Pairwise removal is 4 re-runs only if the pair to test is already known; a k=3 set has three pairs, so an honest estimator that does not know which pair is conflicting costs 3 + 3 = 6 re-runs against exact Shapley's 7, and the proposal never specifies or prices the flagging rule. The title's 'three re-runs, not seven' is also inconsistent with the body, which says single removal is 3 and pairwise is 4.
what_would_fix_it: (1) Put the two estimators on a common scale before comparing, as the entailment check says: calibrate each rule's cutoff to a matched false-deletion rate on E items (or to the same quantile of each estimator's own null distribution measured on the (E,F)/(E,E',F) sets), or report ROC/AUC for W-vs-E discrimination at equal re-runs. Under a matched-FPR comparison the pairwise rule's advantage must come from variance reduction or from the interaction term, which is the claim actually of interest, and P3 becomes a live prediction rather than an arithmetic consequence. (2) Since the proposal proves the two-player Shapley cannot re-order the pair, drop the pruning framing for the pair and instead compare estimators that CAN differ in ranking: single removal vs the interaction-corrected credit c_i + I_ij/2 applied across the three pairs of the set, or single removal vs exact Shapley, on a set where the pair is not known in advance. (3) Specify and price the pair-flagging rule (how a pruner decides which of the three pairs to spend the extra re-run on, and its error rate), so the 4-vs-7 cost claim is measured rather than assumed. (4) Power P5 to confirm, not only to falsify: the equivalence band must exceed the D CI (e.g. 16 seeds on the 96-game subset, or an explicit TOST with a band of 8 net), otherwise 'pairwise recovers exact Shapley' cannot be established by this design. (5) Replace P2's strawman null. A literal duplicate of E adding <=5 net is close to definitional in a prompt whose procedure content is already present; state and cite a mechanism that actually predicts positive dose for a correct item (the compliance trap's repeated-exposure amplification is about a wrong item), or reframe P2 around the interesting quantity, the paraphrase-vs-literal contrast at fixed k. (6) Add a prevalence arm, even a small one: the natural-neighbour class was cut for budget, so 'a single-removal pruner keeps W in most sets' is a statement about planted sets only; a 2-seed count of how often the natural k=3 bank actually co-retrieves a conflicting-procedure neighbour would convert the result from a designed tautology into a claim about real banks.
missing_baseline: A zero-re-run detector on the same 96 sets and the same decision: does an NLI/contradiction check (or a procedure-verb mismatch check, or the retriever's own score/rank margin) between co-retrieved items delete W at a comparable rate for zero LLM re-runs? The entire contribution is stated on a re-run cost axis, yet the plan never asks whether the pair needs to be scored by re-runs at all, and a reviewer will say the cheapest baseline was not run first (the brief's own binding rule). Second omission, also brief-mandated: no learned/proxy scorer arm. The brief requires proxy scores to be evaluated by rank correlation against the interventional ground truth (MemQ-style TD-lambda, RoMeRL-style utility coordinates, usage-decay survival, DIG-style confidence gain), and this proposal reimplements none of them, so it measures an estimator against an estimator with nothing at stake for any deployed scoring system. Third, smaller: no all-pairs (three-pair) variant of the pairwise estimator, which is the correct cost-matched comparator when the conflicting pair is not known a priori.
preprint_collision: No verified collision. The proposal's own check is above average for this round: four classed queries with channel named, IDs given, and an explicit statement that WebSearch was not used. I verified with s2cli (S2+HF, the only channel available; WebSearch is unavailable and WebFetch blocked on this node) the IDs its novelty argument leans on: 2605.05716, 2604.05467, 2607.10608, 2608.07622, 2608.02508, 2410.01649 and 2403.13106 all resolve with matching titles; 2507.04480 failed the `s2cli paper` lookup ('not found') but was returned by my search query with the exact id, date 2025-07-06, PKDD/ECML Workshops, 7 citations, so I count it verified. I could NOT verify 2605.27105, 2605.01302, 2606.25161, 2607.05844, 2608.04574 or 2603.13326; none of them carries the novelty argument. My queries, all answered by the s2cli channel (s2=ok hf=ok on each): (a) 'masking of leave-one-out credit by co-retrieved item interaction agent memory' --recent -> 12 hits, nearest are FocusMem 2608.04530, HiMPO 2606.16285, TreeMem 2605.04811, controllable memory usage 2601.05107; none measures interaction between co-retrieved items, effectively empty for the claim. (b) 'pairwise removal versus single removal interaction non-additivity retrieved documents credit' -> 14 hits, only CUE-R 2604.05467 relevant; otherwise empty. (c) 'Shapley value attribution retrieved documents redundancy synergy retrieval-augmented generation' -> returned 2507.04480 (the closest threat, see above), RAG-E (S2, no arXiv id), shapiq 2410.01649, OddSHAP 2602.01399, joint Shapley 2107.11357. (d) home-vocabulary, no agent/memory words: 'data valuation leave-one-out underestimates value interaction duplicated conflicting training points Shapley' -> Data Shapley 1904.02868, joint Shapley 2107.11357, shapiq 2410.01649, distribution-shift Shapley 2210.10769. (e) 'counterfactual per-item utility pruning wrong memory entries decision error re-run cost agent' --recent -> 4 hits, all counterfactual regret minimization, empty for this claim. Two criticisms of the proposal's check. First, its home-literature query treats shapiq and Shapley-Taylor as merely 'supplying the estimand', but query (d) shows the data-valuation literature is where the claim itself lives: that leave-one-out is biased downward under duplication and mis-signs under complementarity is the standing motivation for Shapley-style valuation, so the sign predictions P1 and P2 are not new claims and the check should have said so rather than logging 'none applied to co-retrieved items'. Second, no query in the check targets its own decision claim (whether a cheaper interaction-aware estimator changes a selection/pruning decision at matched LLM-call cost), which is precisely 2507.04480's stated aim; the check dates that paper as a 'closest named method' hit without noting it is an indexed, cited workshop paper on the cost-vs-exactness tradeoff. The check is therefore thorough on the agent-memory side and thin exactly where the proposal is weakest.
